summary: Abridgment of BERLIN (1858-1859) that keeps all eight verbatim excerpts and the essential arc. The arc runs from the parents' consent, through the Persia gale, England, the Black District, London, Antwerp, the single Berlin lecture, Sumner and Apthorp, and the Gymnasium, to the accidental Beethoven awakening and the Thuringen vow. Cuts fall mainly on the plan's optional units.
acceptable_changes: Cut Captain Judkins, G. P. R. James, the Adelphi coffee-room and the Charles the First tower (optional).
Reduced the Eaton Hall/Grosvenor catalogue to the awe and 'Aristocracy was real' (optional).
Cut the Piccadilly chariots and hatchments. Kept the tall-hats episode, Fleet Street, and the Royal Exchange/Bank of England as the image of insolence (optional).
Cut the Scheldt peasants, Ostade/Teniers, Alva and the 'terribly sober' return to Antwerp (optional).
Cut the daughters-in-law dread and shortened the ironic list of Henry's virtues (optional).
Compressed the Prussian political background (the regent, Bismarck) to the sentence about a scandal every earnest German wanted to reform (optional).
Cut the food and Thiergarten-tramp details, and the 1848 and nobility notes, from the Gymnasium paragraph (optional).
Cut the theatre/opera aside in the by-products paragraph (optional).
risks: Section budgets are approximate. The Sumner/Gymnasium section likely runs over its 733 words, while the Berlin-university section and the by-products/farewell section may run somewhat under. The total should be near 2933 but was not measured.
The period phrase 'derisive Jew laughter of Heine' is kept exactly as in the source, per the plan's risk note.
review_focus: Check that Apthorp's introduction in the Gymnasium setup precedes his Beethoven remark.
Check that the Sumner cabman boast and the poodle/cabman echo both survive for the callback in the ROME chapter.
Check that the Gotterdammerung forward note is preserved and left unelaborated.
Check that the closing ends on the Thuringen proposal and the vow against Berlin.
